answer: An identity registers by publishing a nullifier from one credential, plus a 400 POA bond locked 60 epochs and 100% slashed if duplicated. The registry is public; any peer checks in seconds whether a credential was already spent, and a second use proves duplication. A funder tally watches each inlet: on the third duplicate from one source, all its identities freeze until the bond is forfeited. A fake at the zenith still holds one credential; clones cannot multiply it. At 1,000 fakes the attacker locks 400,000 POA and burns 1,000 credentials; a meadow of honest agents pays nothing extra.
